coach_themes.label: Does not hand out payment plans to an uncertainty objection

examples.issue: After she said there was no way, the rep kept probing savings, credit and income, floated a credit solution and cutting coaching time, even though J. repeatedly said she could not do it.
examples.better: That makes complete sense, J., and I'm not going to push you. Can I send you some free resources and check in with you after your procedure on the 4th?

examples.issue: C. asked about splitting payments and then said he would have to think about it for finances. The rep answered an uncertainty objection with payment options, then improvised a $1K two-session start, texted Kim for it, and sent a payment link, while the real issue (is this worth paying for) was unresolved.
examples.better: Let's set the money aside for a second. If cost were not a factor at all, would you do this? What is the one thing that would keep you from a 10 on whether this is the right step?

examples.issue: When the prospect said she needed to check her financials, the rep immediately offered to split the payment and promised flexibility, answering an uncertainty with a payment plan.
examples.better: Of course, that makes sense. Before we talk about how to make it work, you told me this is the kick you need. On a scale of 1 to 10, how sure are you that this is the right path for you?

examples.issue: J. said he did not know how he felt about the number, and Elly immediately offered an in-house split and ClarityPay. The script says not to hand out payment plans to solve an uncertainty objection, and J. later said the upfront cost did not bother him.
examples.better: That's fair, J.. Before we talk about how to pay for it, let's set the money aside for a second. If cost weren't a factor, do you feel this is the right process to get you to the relationship you told me about?

coach_themes.label: High-level promise of process and visible change, no outcome guarantee

examples.issue: Made outcome promises not in the script: a placement rate and a dates-per-week claim. The script says dating outcomes cannot be guaranteed; promise the process and near-term visible change.
examples.better: I can't promise you an outcome, L., and no honest coach can. What I can promise is a clear, honest read of how you're showing up and visible change in how you date within the first few weeks.

examples.issue: Outcome-adjacent promise in the pitch and the close: citing other people reconnecting with exes. This leans on outcome, where the script promises process and near-term visible change only. Also no 'confidential / recorded / full transparency' frame at the start (C1a to C1d).
examples.better: I can't promise how she responds, nobody can. What I can promise is that after working with Kim you will know exactly what you want to say, whether to say it, and how to show up grounded either way.

examples.issue: Rep quoted client outcome percentages and said Kim attends clients' weddings, which implies a relationship outcome the playbook says cannot be promised.
examples.better: I can't promise you a relationship or a timeline. What I can promise is a clear process, and most people start seeing different responses within the first few weeks.

examples.issue: Rep gave an unverified 80% figure for clients meeting their life partner within a year, which is an outcome promise the script forbids, then later hedged with 'I can't guarantee'.
examples.better: I can't promise you a specific outcome, nobody honestly can. What I can promise is a clear process, and most people start to see visible change in how they show up and the responses they get within the first few weeks.

coach_themes.label: Takes money off the table and checks belief in the process first

examples.issue: When J. said she was recovering financially, the rep said finances were secondary and gave a long reassurance speech, but never ran the 1-10 temperature check or the not-should-I-but-how tie-down. She moved to price without knowing how strongly J. believed in the process.
examples.better: J., taking money completely off the table for a second, on a scale of 1 to 10, how do you feel about the process itself?

examples.issue: When he asked to try a call with Kim first, Elly answered with 'nothing is guaranteed' and 'That has never happened', then invented a $1,000 non-refundable deposit instead of taking money off the table and checking belief in the process.
examples.better: That's a fair thing to want, D.. Before we talk about how it's structured, setting money aside for a second, do you believe Kim's process is the right way for you to get where you want to go?

examples.issue: When he said he did not have the money, Makena offered to break the session up before checking belief, then offered financing again and a Clarity Pay link, and texted Kim for a cheaper plan. Payment plans were used to solve the objection instead of taking money off the table first.
examples.better: I hear you. Let's set the money aside for a second. On a scale of 1 to 10, how confident are you that working with Kim would get you the clarity you're after?

examples.issue: After J. asked for time to process, Elly pushed for about 30 minutes: an improvised $1,000 deposit, 'what if I told you the program was free', guilt framing about holding him accountable, and 'you sound bummed'. She never took money off the table and checked belief in the process.
examples.better: That's completely fair, J., and I respect how you make decisions. Let's book a follow-up for tomorrow so you can sleep on it, and I'll send you a short recap of what we covered so you have it in front of you.

coach_themes.label: Discloses the call is recorded

examples.issue: Rep said the call was confidential but never disclosed that it was being recorded.
examples.better: Everything we talk about is confidential, and just so you know, this call is being recorded.

examples.issue: The prospect volunteered that the meeting was being recorded; the rep never disclosed recording, never asked how much time she had, and the hard stop later forced the price into a rush.
examples.better: J. so you know, this call is recorded and everything you share is confidential. How much time do you have today so we can finish without rushing?

examples.issue: Opening never states the call is confidential or recorded and never invites full transparency, and the goal of the call is not framed and agreed.
examples.better: Everything we talk about today is confidential, and this call is being recorded. I'd love for you to be fully transparent with me so I can point you to the right help. Does that sound good?

examples.issue: Confidentiality was stated but there was no recording disclosure, no credibility line and no invitation to full transparency.
examples.better: Everything we talk about is confidential, and the call is being recorded so Kim can review it before you meet her. I've taken hundreds of these calls, so please be completely open with me. Is that okay?

coach_themes.label: Recommends one tier based on discovery

examples.issue: No single sanctioned tier was recommended. The rep said 'ranging from 3 to 12 months', '7 to 14K', then invented a 6-week, four-session, $2,400 package, then a $1K two-session package. None of those are the sanctioned $3,600 / $7,200 / $14,000 tiers.
examples.better: Based on what you told me about wanting clarity on whether to reach out and how to do it, I would put you in the 3-month bi-weekly program with Kim. That is $3,600.

examples.issue: Elly stated a single price as a 'raised' price with no discovery-based tier recommendation and never asked about financial capacity first. The sanctioned $3,600 bi-weekly tier never came up although he was already paying three coaches and said the amount was beyond his plan.
examples.better: D., you told me you already work with three coaches and you want Kim to fill in what they haven't covered. For that, the fit is bi-weekly one-on-one time with Kim for three months, and the investment is $3,600. How does that sit with you?

examples.issue: The price was dropped after a feature list, with no tie to what he said and no money qualification before the pitch, even though he had volunteered a finance concern earlier. The rep then asked how much he could pay monthly only after he balked.
examples.better: Before I tell you what the investment is, what would feel realistic for you to put toward getting this solved? Based on what you told me about boundaries, attachment and wanting a clear plan, I recommend the three-month program with Kimberly every week. The investment is $7,200.

examples.issue: Rep quoted the whole 7 to 14K range and then invented a 6-week, 4-session $2,400 package that is not one of the sanctioned tiers. Price was said with no recommendation tied to his discovery and no temperature check first.
examples.better: Based on everything you've shared, I'd recommend the three-month program with weekly one-on-one time with Kim. The investment is $7,200.

coach_themes.label: Uses the 1 to 10 scale when the answer is uncertain

examples.issue: Price went out in the same turn as the pitch. There was no temperature check, no 1 to 10 scale and no 'what keeps you from a 10' before the number, even though C. had been visibly back and forth all call and later said he was unsure of the process.
examples.better: Before we talk about the investment, how do you feel about what we just walked through, and on a scale of 1 to 10, how confident are you that this gets you the clarity you want? What would it take to get that to a 9 or 10?

examples.issue: He said he would like to 'sleep on it'. Elly asked what was behind it (good) but when he explained, she did not use the 1 to 10 scale or ask what keeps him from a 9 or 10 before moving on to price.
examples.better: I appreciate you telling me that, D.. On a scale of 1 to 10, how confident are you that this is the right process for you? And what would it take to get that number to a 10?

examples.issue: J.'s answer to the temperature question was hedged ('I think so' then 'the only reason I hesitate'), but Elly resolved it with flexibility reassurance and moved straight to price without the 1 to 10 scale or asking what keeps him from a 9 or 10.
examples.better: On a scale of one to ten, how do you feel about this process as a way to get you to your goal? And what would it take to move that number up to a nine or ten?

examples.issue: She caught a soft 'I think it's worth it' but did not use the 1 to 10 scale or ask what would make it a 9 or 10, and she had already bracketed the conversation with 'Assuming we can kind of figure out the financial side of things'.
examples.better: On a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being I'm in, where are you on working with Kim on this? What would make that a 9 or a 10?

coach_themes.label: Does not correct the belief yet (saves it for the pitch)

examples.issue: Challenged his belief ('you're kind of, like, externalizing') during the doubt question and kept pressing it for several minutes, instead of asking what he thinks is in the way and saving the correction for the pitch. He became defensive ('I'm trying to be neutral').
examples.better: What do you think has been getting in the way of you finding a partner? Take your time. I'm just going to write that down, and I'll come back to it when I show you how Kim works.

examples.issue: After the doubt question the rep argued a diagnosis (hot-and-cold pattern from childhood, 'you probably would have moved on from D. sooner') instead of banking the belief for the pitch, and pushed 'Are you sure?' on commitment before any pitch.
examples.better: That's really helpful, thank you for being so honest about that. I'm going to hold onto that as we keep going. What else do you think has been getting in the way?

examples.issue: After the doubt question the rep corrected his beliefs repeatedly (accountability, traumas, 'you're not taking accountability') and interrupted him, which cost rapport and burned time that belongs to the pitch.
examples.better: Thank you for being so open about that. I'll come back to it when I walk you through how Kimberly helps. What is it about the dating you have been doing that you most want to be different?

examples.issue: Ellie argued with E.'s belief instead of asking the doubt question and moving on. She told her that people who say they cannot find the right person are the ones who stay single forever, which preceded the 'judged' comment.
examples.better: What do you think has been getting in the way of finding the right person so far? Thank you, that helps. Is there anything else you feel has been standing in the way?

coach_themes.label: Asks what it has been costing them, beyond dating

examples.issue: The cost-of-inaction question drew 'I've accepted the fact that I'm alone' and the rep answered with a mini-lecture instead of asking a sharper cost question using her own words about wasting her fifties.
examples.better: You said you don't want to waste your fifties being alone. If another year goes by with the same pick-me patterns, what does that cost you?

examples.issue: Cost of inaction was asked once and he said he would find a partner anyway; Elly accepted that and moved on without going deeper on what staying stuck has cost him beyond dating.
examples.better: You've said it's been a goal for six years. What has that waiting cost you, beyond dating, in how you feel day to day?

examples.issue: After summarising his situation she went straight to the offer. She never asked what the uncertainty has been costing him, why now, a magic wand, or a picture a year out, so there was no urgency or value built before price.
examples.better: What has this uncertainty been costing you, beyond the relationship itself? And if this were resolved a year from now, what would that picture look like?

examples.issue: No why-now or cost-of-inaction question was asked. Instead the rep asked a closed question about staying in the same spot, which gave him an easy out ('status quo can go on'), then issued a takeaway before pitching.
examples.better: What made you decide to take this call now instead of six months ago? And what has being stuck here been costing you, beyond dating?

coach_themes.label: Tie-down: 'not should I, but how do I make this work'

examples.issue: No tie-down from 'should I' to 'how do I make this work'. The rep restated the same fastest-route argument at 1:20, 4:01 and 5:41 instead of asking him to define what his own plan looks like and how long he would give it.
examples.better: Let's say you put yourself out there on your own for the next three months. What would have to be true at the end of it for you to say it worked, and what happens to the five years you just told me work consumed if it doesn't?

examples.issue: After recommending the six-month tier on discovery, the rep reversed when J. said 'do I need six months?', telling her it is 'not more of a need' and asking for the 7200 instead of using the tie-down on how to make the recommended plan work.
examples.better: You told me this pattern has been with you for about 20 years and you want to build a family. That is exactly why I pointed you to the six months. The question isn't whether you should do it, it's how we make it work for you. What would have to be true for the six months to feel doable?

examples.issue: On the think-about-it objection she turned his perfectionism and decision style into a pressure point ('24 hours turns into 48, turns into a week, turns into, oh, now it's the new year, new me') and then pushed with 'is it the case that you don't have the money', rather than a clean tie-down from 'should I' to 'how do I make this work'.
examples.better: R., you told me this is the decision you want to make, so it's not a question of whether, it's how we make it work for you financially. What number would feel comfortable to put down today?

examples.issue: After 'I might hold off on that for right now' she took money off the table once, but his answer was muddled and she moved straight into payment plans instead of getting a clear yes on the process and then the tie-down.
examples.better: No worries at all. Set the money aside for a second: if the investment were not a factor, is this what you want to do? If yes, then the question is not should you do this, it is how do we make it work.

coach_themes.label: Paints getting started before revealing the investment

examples.issue: Money was never qualified before the pitch (no question about whether he is in a position to invest). Credit score and cash on hand were asked only after he balked at the number, and the answer ($500) disqualified him 20 minutes after the price was named.
examples.better: Before I walk you through how Kim works, one honest question: if this turns out to be the right fit, is investing in your dating life something you're in a position to do right now?

examples.issue: Money and decision capacity were never qualified before the pitch. Finances only surfaced after price, and the rep then asked about it in a roundabout way ('you have the investment, and it's just a matter...').
examples.better: If Kim tells you this is the right path, is there anything that would get in the way of getting started, financially or otherwise? Is anyone else involved in the decision?

examples.issue: After the pitch the rep went straight to the tuition with no step painting what getting started looks like, and did it at minute 58 knowing the prospect had a meeting at the top of the hour.
examples.better: Here is what happens next if we go ahead: we get you onboarded today and book your first one-on-one with Kim this week, so you are working on that cycle right away. Does that feel like the right next step?

examples.issue: Price was revealed (both the 6-month and 3-month tiers) in the opening seconds of the pitch, before any pillar and before a temperature check, so H. heard $14K and $7,200 with no value built and then spent the rest of the call on cost.
examples.better: Before I get into the investment, let me walk you through exactly how Kim works with her clients. [after pillars] On a scale of 1 to 10, how do you feel about this process for you? ... If we were to get you started, the first thing that happens is your onboarding call with Kim, and within the first few weeks you'd start to see different responses. Now, based on everything you've shared, the plan I'd recommend for you is the 3-month plan at $7,200.

coach_themes.label: Asks how they feel about the process

examples.issue: Price was stated ($3,600 for six, then $1,000 for one session) with no pitch of the process and no temperature check. The process-feel question only came after he said he could not pay, and money was qualified only after the price.
examples.better: Based on everything you've shared, how do you feel about the process I just walked you through?

examples.issue: Price was stated at the end of discovery with no transition, no walk-through of how Kim helps, and no permission. The pitch came after the price, so he heard the number with no value attached. She also listed 6-month, 3-month and 12-month plans together and muddled which was $7,200.
examples.better: Based on everything you've shared about building confidence and finally getting a woman's honest read on how you show up, can I walk you through how Kim works with someone in your spot? Then we'll talk about the investment.

examples.issue: Price was introduced straight out of the pillars ('So what this actually comes with, so there's a few different plans') with no temperature check, no 1 to 10, and no paint of getting started. His first question about the process came only after the price, and she never asked what he had available.
examples.better: Before I share the investment, based on everything we've gone over, how do you feel about the process?

examples.issue: After he said it would not work, she argued with the Bible and free-will analogy, asked whether people in healthy relationships got there by feeling ready, and used 'if you truly valued yourself'. He later asked whether that was why she would not let him hang up. A low-intent prospect should be released cleanly.
examples.better: I appreciate you being honest about that, J.. It sounds like the timing isn't right, and I'd rather you be sure than rush into something. If that changes, reach back out and we'll pick it back up.

coach_themes.label: States the price and stays silent

examples.issue: Revealed price and named two tiers (3 months at $7,200 and 'over 14K') before the pitch, before any 1-10 check, and offered to 'break it up' in the same breath. The prospect first said he did not know the number, then reacted to it as a surprise at 01:09:38.
examples.better: L., based on everything you told me about reading women and wanting to stop wasting time, I'm going to walk you through exactly how Kim works with men like you. At the end I'll ask how it feels, and only then we'll talk about the investment.

examples.issue: Price was stated, then financing and a request for an amount he could pay today were added in the same breath. No silence after the number, and the payment solution came before any objection existed.
examples.better: Based on everything you shared about the anxiety, the confidence and wanting a real plan, I recommend the three-month program with weekly one-on-ones with Kimberly. The investment is $7,200.

examples.issue: Stated both the $14K and $7,200 prices in the middle of the pitch, before the four pillars were delivered and before any temperature check. The rest of the pitch then ran after price was already on the table, and he said the number was 'a little bit more than what I was expecting to spend' at the first chance.
examples.better: R., that's everything Kim does. Before we talk about the investment, how do you feel about the process, and on a scale of 1 to 10, how confident are you that it would help you?

examples.issue: He answered the price with 'I've saved up' and 'what else am I going to invest in but myself', and Ellie immediately reached for the 'few years down the road' line and then in-house and ClarityPay plans, though he had not raised a budget objection. She did not state the price and stay quiet.
examples.better: I'm glad to hear that, N.. Based on everything you told me, the three-month program with weekly one-on-one calls with Kim is the right fit. Would you like to get started today?

coach_themes.label: States the call is confidential

examples.issue: Opened with small talk and straight into a question; no confidentiality, no recording disclosure, no credibility line, no invitation to be fully open, and no agreed goal for the call.
examples.better: Before we start, I want you to know this call is completely confidential, and it is being recorded so Kim can review it before she meets you. I've taken hundreds of these calls, so please be fully open with me. The goal today is to understand what you want, and if it makes sense, walk you through how Kim could help. Does that work for you?

examples.issue: To reassure her that nothing is required, rep named another client and described his severe anxiety, which breaches the confidentiality she promised at the start.
examples.better: There's nothing you have to do that you don't want to. Some people come in not wanting to be on apps at all, and Kim tailors the work to whatever you're ready for. Your onboarding call is where you tell her what you do and don't want.

examples.issue: Opened with small talk and straight into the problem question, with no confidentiality statement, no recording disclosure, no credibility line and no agreed goal for the call.
examples.better: Everything we talk about is confidential, and the call is being recorded so Kim can review it. I've taken hundreds of these calls, so please be completely open with me. The goal is to understand where you're at, and if it makes sense, show you how Kim could help. Does that work?

examples.issue: Checked availability and referenced the setter, but gave no confidentiality statement, no recording disclosure, no credibility line and no agreed goal for the call.
examples.better: Everything we talk about is confidential, and the call is being recorded so Kim can review it. I've taken hundreds of these calls, so please be completely open with me. The goal is to understand where you're at and, if it makes sense, show you how Kim can help. Does that work for you?

coach_themes.label: Ties the recommendation to what they said

examples.issue: Rep recommended the 14k six-month tier right after J. described supporting her daughter and playing catch-up. The recommendation was tied to anxiety and frustration, not to her situation, and financial capacity was never asked before the pitch.
examples.better: Before I show you what I'd recommend, can I ask what you'd be comfortable investing in yourself if this is the right fit?

examples.issue: The rep named the three-month one-on-one tier but did not tie it to what J. said she needed, so the price landed as a number instead of an answer to her problem.
examples.better: Based on what you told me, five years stuck in this situationship and needing the kick in the pants and direction, I would recommend working with Kim one-on-one every week for three months. That is $7,200.

examples.issue: The $7,200 was stated flatly with no link back to E.'s goal, followed straight by an offer to split it. No recommendation framing and no pause after the number.
examples.better: Based on what you told me about wanting a committed marriage and not wanting to stay too long where it is not moving, I would recommend weekly one-on-one time with Kim for three months. The investment is $7,200.

examples.issue: She named two options (six months at 14k, then three months of 'around 12 sessions') without tying the recommendation to what he said or stating the three-month price. He then assumed about $7,000 and the card was charged with no amount spoken.
examples.better: Based on what you told me, needing validation and not knowing how you're showing up, the three-month plan with weekly one-on-one time with Kim is the right fit. The investment is $7,200.

coach_themes.label: Pillar 1, The Honest Read, tied to what they've tried

examples.issue: The pillars were read as a generic list and not tied to what he had tried. He had told her he had done years of mindset work with three coaches and answered the pitch with 'that is something that, um, most of my work has done'.
examples.better: D., you've done years of inner work with three coaches. The first thing Kim does is The Honest Read: she looks at exactly what you've tried and why it hasn't turned into a partner yet. Then The Reset and Read & Lead take the inner work you've already done and put it into how you actually show up and date.

examples.issue: No four-pillar pitch. Rep went from his headspace answer straight to price and a loose description of what Kim would do, never tying the Honest Read to what he had tried (nothing, no therapy, no coach).
examples.better: Kim's process has four parts. The first is the Honest Read, a professional female perspective on what is actually happening with KC, which you said you can't get from your guy friends.

examples.issue: The pitch was a generic three-phase framework (clarity, transformation, implementation) read as a list of features. It was not the four pillars and nothing was tied to what E. said she had tried (staying too long in relationships that were not moving ahead, hanging on to the radio host). The price then recommended a tier without tying it to her words.
examples.better: The first piece is what we call The Honest Read. You told me you tend to hang on too long when a relationship is not moving ahead. Kim gives you an honest read on what has been happening, so you can spot it sooner and not spend years on it again.

examples.issue: Pitch was a read-out of a three-phase framework and a feature list, not the four pillars, and it was not tied to her words (can't tell if she's choosing wrong or showing up wrong, friends say she is standoffish).
examples.better: You told me you can't figure out if you're choosing the wrong person or showing up differently. The first thing Kim gives you is an Honest Read, a professional's eye on what you're actually doing, so you stop guessing.

coach_themes.label: Does not dump all tiers

examples.issue: When J. asked 'What are the other ones?', the rep listed the 3-month tier at half price instead of holding on the single recommendation, and called 'the two tier'.
examples.better: I'd rather keep you focused on what I'm recommending for you, the six-month plan at $14,000, because it fits a pattern you've had for 20 years. If it doesn't feel right after we talk it through, we can look at the other options together.

examples.issue: She named several plans (6 months around 14K, 3 months, 12 months) and said starting with the 6 months would show progress, then quoted $7,200. This is a tier dump with a contradictory recommendation.
examples.better: Based on what you told me about confidence and eight to ten years of nothing sticking, I'd recommend the three-month program with weekly calls with Kim. The investment is $7,200.

examples.issue: Rep quoted the three-month tier at $7,200, then the six-month tier at 13,900 (sanctioned is $14,000), then asked her to pick, and later offered credit from the first three months toward the second. No single recommendation tied to her discovery.
examples.better: Based on what you told me, four years on the hamster wheel and wanting to feel settled, I'd recommend the six-month program with weekly one-on-one time with Kim. The investment is $14,000.

examples.issue: Before any pitch or temperature check she quoted the 6-month 14K and the 3-month $7,200 and added 'we can break it up if needed'. That dumps two tiers, reveals price into uncertainty and offers a payment plan before any objection.
examples.better: Based on what you told me about wanting a marriage-minded relationship and not knowing how to keep the connection going after a first date, I would recommend the three-month program with Kim every week. Let me walk you through what that includes first.

coach_themes.label: Reflects their situation back and gets permission to walk through how Kim helps

examples.issue: Makena told him he had led himself to the answer and that she 'didn't really even say anything', then asked only whether there was anything else. She never reflected his situation back (overthinking, hard to let go, not trusting his own judgment) or asked permission to walk him through how Kim helps.
examples.better: From everything you've shared, you overthink, it's hard for you to let people go, and you're not yet trusting your own judgment. Did I get that right? Can I walk you through how Kim helps with exactly that?

examples.issue: M. told her his goal was strategies to present himself differently, that he freezes approaching women he likes and cannot read signals. Ellie never reflected that back or got permission, and the pitch was a generic three-phase list with nothing tied to his words. His layoff and 'uncertainties' also went unexplored until after the pitch.
examples.better: Let me make sure I have this right. You freeze when you want to approach someone, you are not sure how to read signals, and you want strategies to present yourself so you stop scaring people off. Did I miss anything? Can I walk you through how Kim helps with exactly that?

examples.issue: The rep knew T. had a hard stop at 12:30, but spent about 27 minutes on relationship history and tangents (clutter, family) and reached the end with 'we're kind of at time here' without a transition or the process.
examples.better: You have until 12:30, so I'm going to keep us moving so we have time at the end for me to show you exactly how Kim helps. Based on what you've shared, can I walk you through how she would work with you?

examples.issue: No reflect-back and permission to walk through how Kim helps. The four pillars and the delivery (group calls twice a week, library, community, 1:1 time) were never presented. Fragments of the pitch were dropped into discovery answers, and the first real step was jumping to asking him to book a call.
examples.better: Let me make sure I have this right. You have been single eleven years, you are putting yourself out there again, you worry you are not ready for a real relationship, and you want an honest female perspective. Did I miss anything? Can I walk you through how Kim helps with exactly that?

coach_themes.label: Asks them to paint the picture a year from now

examples.issue: Discovery never asked for the desired picture, why it matters or a magic wand, and the cost question was a yes-or-no on headspace, so the pitch had little emotional fuel.
examples.better: If we were talking a year from now and this was completely figured out, what would that look like for you?

examples.issue: No picture of the future and no magic wand. After he said he overthinks and does not trust his judgment, she moved to her own opinion instead of asking what life looks like if that were solved.
examples.better: If you could trust your own call without second-guessing, what would your life look like a year from now?

examples.issue: She never asked him to describe a year from now or what he would most look forward to, so the pitch was not tied to a vision he had described; discovery spent most of its time on zodiac and politics instead.
examples.better: Let's say it's a year from now and this worked exactly how you wanted it to. What does your life look like, and what part are you most looking forward to?

examples.issue: After he confirmed the goal is a long-term partner, she moved on to commitment mechanics and never asked him to paint the picture a year from now, why it matters or what he looks forward to most. Without a desired picture there was nothing for the gap to attach to.
examples.better: If we are a year from now and you are in the relationship you want, what does that look like? And why is that important to you?

coach_themes.label: Delivery: group calls twice weekly, library, community, 1:1 for paid tiers

examples.issue: When S. said she did not want group coaching, Brianna immediately offered to 'take that out' and called the community 'not necessary', discounting part of what the paid tiers include instead of positioning it.
examples.better: That's good to know, S.. Your one-on-one time with Kim is where your personal work happens, and the group calls are an extra you can use or not as you feel ready.

examples.issue: The pitch was a long spiel on a three-phase framework plus a list of coaching features, and the delivery described only weekly 1:1 sessions and email support. Group coaching calls, the education library and the community were never mentioned, and L. had to ask what kind of service it was.
examples.better: Here's how it works. Alongside your weekly one-on-one with Kim, you get group coaching calls twice a week, the full education library, and the community, so you're supported every day, not just once a week.

examples.issue: The pitch described weekly sessions but never covered group coaching twice a week, the education library or the community.
examples.better: Along with your one-on-one time with Kim, you also get group coaching calls twice a week, the full education library and the community.

examples.issue: When he asked whether the work is individual or in a group she answered 'No, no, no group', but group coaching calls twice a week, the education library and the community are part of every tier. Delivery was described as a weekly one-hour session only.
examples.better: Your main time is one-on-one with Kim every week, and on top of that you get group coaching calls twice a week, the full education library, and the community.

coach_themes.label: Lets silence breathe instead of rushing

examples.issue: He said his father died of alcohol, that he drinks more around his birthday while alone, and 'I haven't killed myself yet'. She said 'Sorry to hear that', asked 'Do you drink a lot?' and moved on to loneliness without checking in on the self-harm remark.
examples.better: L., I want to stop on something you just said. You said you haven't killed yourself yet. Are you having any thoughts of hurting yourself right now?

examples.issue: H. disclosed she was raped two weeks before her wedding, and later a sexual assault and stalking and a day she called her therapist to avoid spiraling. Rep gave one line of sympathy and moved to the next question, then used the disclosure as sales leverage ('someone like D.').
examples.better: Thank you for trusting me with that, H., I know that's not easy to say out loud. Take whatever time you need. Are you okay to keep going, or would you like a minute?

examples.issue: Right after L. said she had been 'pretty suicidal in my early 30s', the rep asked 'would you say you're okay with the situation you're in with dating' and stepped away to charge her computer. There was no acknowledgement, no pause, and the call went on to the sale.
examples.better: Thank you for trusting me with that, L.. I'm really glad you're in a better place now. Take your time. How are you feeling right now as we talk about this?

coach_themes.label: Asks the biggest thing not working in dating/relationships

examples.issue: Discovery skipped the biggest-problem question, what he has tried and how it went, and the where-it-falls-apart probe was only about the one recent date. The pitch could not be tied to what he had tried, so 'is it worth it, could I do it on my own' had no answer.
examples.better: What's the biggest thing that's not working for you in dating right now? And what have you tried so far to change that, and how did it go?

examples.issue: The prospect offered 40 minutes and said the matter weighs on her heavily, but the rep used none of it. A first discovery question here would have deepened commitment for Sunday and given Kim notes.
examples.better: Let's use the next few minutes so Sunday goes straight to what Kim can do for you. What is the biggest thing not working in your dating life right now?

examples.issue: The biggest-thing-not-working question was never asked in a way that moved her off the phone story, so roughly the first 15 minutes produced no clear dating problem, only a fixed physical type, one date in 2026 and a limerence pattern.
examples.better: Setting the phone aside for a moment, what is the biggest thing that's not working in your dating life right now?

coach_themes.label: Handles what keeps them from 9 or 10 before price

examples.issue: He said 6 or 7, then 7 or 8, and said 'until I've tried it, I don't know'. The rep argued with the number ('Why don't you see yourself in that?') instead of finding what stood between him and a 9 or 10, and then went to price anyway.
examples.better: That's a fair answer, and nobody can know until they try it. What is the one thing that would move you from a 7 or 8 to a 9 or 10 on the process?

examples.issue: After the 7 she asked about the fear behind it and moved on, then when S. asked for the price three times she stalled and made it conditional on readiness. The 9 or 10 gap was never closed, and the withholding felt like pressure to S..
examples.better: You deserve a straight answer and I am not hiding anything. You told me you are a 7 because of the unknowns, so let me close that gap first. What is the one thing that would make you a 9 or 10 about starting with Kim now?

examples.issue: The scale check was the right move, but S. did not give a number ('I feel like I can only know once I communicate with her more'). Brianna restated it as 'you think it would work', moved on, and revealed the price within two minutes. Nothing was done about what kept her from a 9 or 10, so the price landed on an unresolved doubt.
examples.better: That's fair, S.. If you had to put a number on it today, would it be closer to a 6, a 7 or an 8? And what would need to be true for it to feel like a 9 or 10?

coach_themes.label: Asks why now vs six months ago

examples.issue: She argued against buying, asking why he does not just figure it out on his own, listen to friends, wait for his friend's opinion, or trust his own judgment. Questions meant to find why now ended up handing him reasons not to invest, and she never asked what it has been costing him.
examples.better: What made you decide to reach out today rather than six months ago, and what has not knowing what to do been costing you?

examples.issue: The call ended before any why-now, cost or desired-outcome question. The one broad question at 14:41 was a compound question about every phase of dating.
examples.better: S., what has made now the time to get help with this, instead of six months ago?

coach_themes.label: Frames the goal of the call and gets agreement

examples.issue: No confidentiality or recording disclosure, no credibility line and no agreed goal. T.'s stated goal was to change one woman's no into a yes, and the rep never reset that expectation, leaving a mis-selling risk and a prospect aiming at the wrong outcome.
examples.better: Everything we talk about is confidential, and the call is being recorded so Kim can review it. I've taken hundreds of these calls, so please be completely open with me. I want to make sure we're aligned: Kim's work is about you becoming the most confident, attractive version of yourself for the right woman, not about changing one particular woman's answer. Is that something you want?

examples.issue: She framed the long call as time to 'get you onboarded and like go through payment', mentioning payment before any discovery and presenting a sale as the expected result.
examples.better: I like to leave a full hour so we can really understand your situation, and then see if working with Kim makes sense for you. If it does, we will talk about next steps then.

coach_themes.label: Asks what they think has been getting in the way

examples.issue: Never asked what L. thinks has been getting in the way, what she has tried, or her weekly dating mechanics. L. said 'I'm really not putting myself out there at all' and the rep moved on, so there was no belief of hers to build the pitch around.
examples.better: L., what do you think has been getting in the way of meeting someone? And what have you tried so far to meet people, on the app or in person?

examples.issue: Instead of asking an open doubt question, Elly told him what was in his way ('you'd agree with me, right? That the reason you've kind of stayed stuck is because you haven't really had the right guidance') and repeated 'would you agree' several times, which he named as leading questions.
examples.better: What do you think has been getting in the way of the relationship you want?

exemplary.quote: So, let's say in the next 3 to 6 months, Kim is able to help you get the extra support to… Gain the confidence to set yourself up for success with dating, and more importantly, actually, be able to read women better and show up better for them.
exemplary.why: Clean magic-wand setup in the prospect's own goal language, and it got a direct answer ('probably everything').

exemplary.quote: Let's say, like, you don't make the change, and as a result, you don't put yourself in the best position possible to actually meet your partner.
exemplary.why: Cost-of-inaction question that moves him from abstract to personal consequences.

exemplary.quote: What would you, like, most… what would you most look forward to, like, having someone fun and genuine to share your life with?
exemplary.why: Re-asks and rephrases when the first attempt did not land, using his own words 'fun and genuine'.

exemplary.quote: really how I just structure these calls is to get a good understanding of, again, where you're at right now, what your goals are, and what you would like to do as far as maybe working with Kim or not, see if that aligns.
exemplary.why: Frames the goal of the call, offers a no-pressure out, and asks for agreement.

exemplary.quote: finances, we can, you know, touch on and work with, but I'm more concerned, like, right now, if this actually feels like a good fit for you.
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and checks belief in the process first; it only needed the 1-10 follow-up.

exemplary.quote: Why are you looking support with this now, specifically, if whether or not you should have this conversation with Charlotte?
exemplary.why: Asks why now directly and ties it to his stated dilemma; surfaces the C. W. no-contact history.

exemplary.quote: let's say 3, 6 months from now, nothing really changes for you, and you're still kind of having these, like, doubts and thoughts of whether or not you should reach out to her.
exemplary.why: Cost-of-inaction question in the prospect's own terms, and she redirects when he answers about the ex instead of himself.

exemplary.quote: Before we get into, like, the finances and everything, is this something that you actually feel like will help you, like, gain the clarity in having that conversation and…
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and checks belief in the process first, which is the script's first move on a price objection.

exemplary.quote: what do you feel like that this has, you know, actually been costing you?
exemplary.why: Asks the cost question and widens it beyond dating, which drew out emotional investment and fear of dying alone.

exemplary.quote: paint me the picture. Okay. If we're talking, I mean, let's say a year from now and this, what we do here, this went exactly how you'd want it to go.
exemplary.why: Clean future-pacing question that gets her to describe peace and a go-to person in her own words.

exemplary.quote: let's take, you know, remove ourself from the price, like with the actual self and what we do.
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and checks belief in the process when the first price question came up; she answered yes.

exemplary.quote: is this something that you genuinely believe can help you meet your ideal partner and start attracting people that actually will make you feel loved and peace and everything we kind of talked about?
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and re-anchors on belief in the process using her own words.

exemplary.quote: So, with therapy, I know they probably give you some actionable steps, but they're not necessarily, like, experts in dating.
exemplary.why: Ties the Honest Read pillar directly to what she has already tried.

exemplary.quote: She filled me in a little bit on your goals, I read your application, but I'd love to hear from you first.
exemplary.why: Shows prep so she feels seen, then hands her the floor.

exemplary.quote: why do you feel like, yeah, now I am ready to, you know, draw that line in the sand and really start, you know, pushing towards my goal of finding a relationship.
exemplary.why: Asks why now directly and draws out concrete reasons (cleared family, money and career first).

exemplary.quote: So I guess, you know, what's kind of behind you wanting to put some more time in between?
exemplary.why: Isolates the real reason behind 'sleep on it' with an open question rather than arguing.

exemplary.quote: I'm curious, like, why is it so important for you to like, figure out the situation rather than just like moving on
exemplary.why: Tests the strength of his motivation instead of accepting the stated goal, and draws out the bond and future he sees with her.

exemplary.quote: when you say like figure out this relationship, is it to figure out like, whether or not you should keep moving forward or with her or like how to navigate it?
exemplary.why: Pins down what he actually means by clarity before going further.

exemplary.quote: what has shifted now that makes you say, like, yeah, I'm really ready to make this a priority
exemplary.why: Direct why-now question that pulled out the leave of absence and the shift in priorities.

exemplary.quote: what is life going to look like for you then?
exemplary.why: Paints the future picture and gets his own words about feeling peaceful and stable.

exemplary.quote: what happens if we continue to keep doing what we're doing?
exemplary.why: Cost-of-inaction question that drew out 'nothing's going to change' in his own words.

exemplary.quote: If you could fix your situation right now that you're in, and three to six months, where would you be?
exemplary.why: Clean future-pacing question that got a concrete picture of companionship and a healthy partner.

exemplary.quote: Are you confident that this program from 1 to 10, if you can tell me, will help you out?
exemplary.why: Uses the 1 to 10 scale before price and surfaced a strong 9 or 10.

exemplary.quote: But Emily caught me up to speed a little bit on your goals, but I'd love to kind of hear from you directly first.
exemplary.why: References the setter notes so he feels seen, then hands the floor to him.

exemplary.quote: What makes you want to get support with this now, rather than just kind of, like, figuring out on your own, or just keeping things as is?
exemplary.why: Clean why-now question that surfaced his real reason (cannot read cues, cannot talk to friends).

exemplary.quote: what happens if, you know, you decide to, you do anything different. You decide to, you know, not make a change.
exemplary.why: Cost-of-inaction question that asks for her reality if nothing changes, a good model for the C6b prompt.

exemplary.quote: do you feel like what we do here is something that could genuinely help you and work for you?
exemplary.why: Direct belief check after the pitch, followed by a 'why do you say yes' to hear her own reasons.

exemplary.quote: So, I read your application, Emily and Kim filled me in a little bit on your situation, but I'd love to hear from you first.
exemplary.why: Uses the setter and application notes so he feels seen, then hands the floor to him.

exemplary.quote: Feel if the next 6 months go by, and you don't necessarily, like, learn the tools necessary to, like, communicate effectively in these relationships to actually build that.
exemplary.why: Segment-aware cost-of-inaction question that drew out his self-disappointment in his own words.

exemplary.quote: You think? You sound a little bit uncertain, which is totally fine. But is there something that, like, you don't feel will work for you?
exemplary.why: Names the hedge calmly and asks what would not work, which brought out his 'can't put a price on that' answer.

exemplary.quote: what really kind of made you want to decide to do something now, as opposed to like maybe like six months ago
exemplary.why: Clean why-now question that contrasts with the cost of waiting.

exemplary.quote: none of these things are telling you the truth about how you're actually showing up, right?
exemplary.why: Ties the Honest Read directly to the therapy, apps and content she has already tried.

exemplary.quote: So like money aside, like you do feel like everything makes sense to you, would actually help you.
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and checks belief in the program before dealing with price.

exemplary.quote: Why, why do you feel like it hasn't happened yet?
exemplary.why: Direct doubt question that gets him articulating his own beliefs about what is in the way.

exemplary.quote: What kind of, what circumstances, just walk me through situations or circumstances that it's come up where you've wished that you had someone there.
exemplary.why: Concrete spillover probe that gets real moments instead of generalities.

exemplary.quote: And you said there might be some more things like deep seated. Like, what, what do you mean by that?
exemplary.why: Picks up his own phrase and asks him to define it in his words.

exemplary.quote: why is this something that you want to do now, rather than waiting, like, another couple of years, or still trying to figure it out on your own?
exemplary.why: Why-now question that draws out his stated reason for acting.

exemplary.quote: is this something that you actually feel will help you gain confidence in dating and eventually get better outcomes?
exemplary.why: Process temperature check before settling the money question.

exemplary.quote: the finances weren't a factor, like, would you 100% be in on this?
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and checks belief in the process.

exemplary.quote: And if you could wave like a magic wand, I just want to know, and fix all the problems that you're having at the moment.
exemplary.why: Opens the magic-wand picture cleanly and led to a specific outcome (talk to anyone without anxiety, be in a relationship).

exemplary.quote: And what would need to happen for you to be at a 9 or 10?
exemplary.why: Right scale follow-up for an 7 or 8 answer; the gap is that she did not hold it long enough.

exemplary.quote: Before we kind of get into ways to break it down, like monthly payments, stuff like that, I just want to make sure, like, the process that we have here, like, do you genuinely believe, like, this could help you meet your ideal partner and help attract better people into your life?
exemplary.why: Takes money off the table and checks belief in the process before any payment talk, exactly as the script asks.

exemplary.quote: You said I think so, which sounds, like, not 100% certain, which is fine. Is there anything that you don't think or you're unsure of that, like, won't be helpful for you?
exemplary.why: Catches the hedge ('I think so') instead of accepting it as a yes, and invites the real doubt.

exemplary.quote: what happens for you if… you continue to overanalyze these relationships, or stay single, in the next 6 months to a year?
exemplary.why: Cost-of-inaction question using his own pattern (overanalyzing) and a concrete time frame.

exemplary.quote: we wave a magic wand, right, and this just isn't a problem anymore.
exemplary.why: Magic wand question done cleanly, and it drew out what she wants to stop doing (second-guessing every text).

exemplary.quote: what do you feel like, you know, that's actually been costing you?
exemplary.why: Cost question that reaches beyond dating, and the rep waited for the answer.

exemplary.quote: What's the part that you're most looking forward to?
exemplary.why: Asks what part of the future she is most looking forward to, setting up the pitch.

exemplary.quote: why don't you trust your own judgment to make this decision?
exemplary.why: Surfaces the real issue under the situationship (self-trust) and gives the pitch something to attach to.

exemplary.quote: what are you holding on to?
exemplary.why: Goes beneath the surface pattern of not letting people go to the emotional driver, a good segment-aware cost question.

exemplary.quote: So Emily kind of filled me in on your situation, but I don't want to assume anything.
exemplary.why: References the setter's notes so he feels seen and still invites his own version.

exemplary.quote: when you say confidence, what do you mean by that confidence?
exemplary.why: Asks him to define his own word and surfaces the height, age and validation issues behind it.

exemplary.quote: It's not because you're too old or you're short. It's because nobody's given you the truth on how you're actually showing up.
exemplary.why: Pillar 1 tied directly to what he said was getting in his way, in a direct tone he said he likes.

exemplary.quote: you being as transparent as possible with me, it, all it does is, is it really helps me get the full picture
exemplary.why: Invites full transparency and says why it helps him, which got a very open answer on his history.

exemplary.quote: what is going to happen, right, the other side of the coin, if you don't take action, right, and you continue doing things the way that you've been doing them
exemplary.why: Gives permission to take time and asks for the cost of staying the same, rather than rushing the answer.

exemplary.quote: Like, what do you think that standing in your own way has actually been costing you? Like, not just in dating, right?
exemplary.why: Direct cost question that widens beyond dating, even with a guarded prospect.

exemplary.quote: Who do you want to become? Who is that? How does he look? How does he talk?
exemplary.why: Future-picture prompt in the prospect's own identity language, and it produced his strongest, most specific answer.

exemplary.quote: What do you feel like would keep you from being a 9 or 10?
exemplary.why: Runs the scale and, when he said 7 to 8, asks what stands between him and a 9 or 10 before price.

exemplary.quote: what do you feel like is personally getting in the way for you?
exemplary.why: Clean doubt question that puts the cause in his own words.

exemplary.quote: did you find that you made progress
exemplary.why: Asks how the prior coaching went, which surfaces the real burned-in-past concern.

exemplary.quote: do you feel like you have to be miserable to want to change something in your life?
exemplary.why: Reframes his 'I'm not miserable' so he can admit he wants change.

exemplary.quote: if you could wave a wand and this wasn't an issue anymore for you with dating, what do you feel like changes?
exemplary.why: Clean magic-wand question that gets her future in her own words.

exemplary.quote: Do like what's the part you're really most looking forward to?

review.reason: Highest script score: use it in training
review.summary: J., 43, a single California MFT and 12-step sober woman, wants a partner and a child and keeps choosing emotionally unavailable men out of abandonment fear. Brianna ran a strong, near-complete discovery and pitch with a 10 out of 10 temperature check, recommended the six-month tier, but then walked her down to the 3-month tier by dropping her own recommendation, and J. signed the 3-month plan on the call.

review.reason: Highest script score: use it in training
review.summary: U., 29, an IT worker on a US visa who grew up in India and has little dating experience, wants help after nine months of ghosting on Hinge. Brianna ran a strong, near-complete discovery, pitch and 9.5 temperature check, but quoted the 6-month $14K tier labelled 'Tier 1' to a prospect who expected $3-4K from the setter, then improvised a $3,400 three-month bi-weekly plan after ClarityPay declined him. He signed that plan on the call.

review.reason: Highest script score: use it in training
review.summary: D., a 21-year-old recent community college graduate between jobs, has never had a real relationship, gets one-sided or ghosted outcomes from women, and links it to guardedness and a hard relationship with his late father. Brianna ran a very long, emotional discovery, pitched well with a 7 to 8 on the scale, then recommended the $14,000 six-month tier without ever qualifying money; once he said he had no savings and no bank account she steered him toward opening credit cards for a future payment plan, and the call ended with no follow-up booked.

review.reason: Highest script score: use it in training
review.summary: S. is a single therapist (independent contractor) in her 30s, four days out from a three-month relationship that ended after what looked like a healthy start, who wants marriage and a family and tried seven months of bi-weekly dating coaching that felt too much like therapy. Brianna ran a thorough discovery, pitched the four pillars and used the 1 to 10 check well, but quoted $14K with no budget qualification and then chased a stated $250-a-session ceiling with an improvised $3,400 tier, ClarityPay and an in-house $500/month plan. S. said she needed to review her finances and a Tuesday 2 pm check-in was booked.

review.reason: Highest script score: use it in training
review.summary: J., 53, divorced after 22 years, estranged from her daughter, five years in a fizzling situationship and off the apps, wants a steady boyfriend and a way to break the cycle. Ellie ran a solid discovery but rushed the pitch, quoted client success percentages, and named $7,200 at minute 58 when the prospect had a work meeting; the budget doubt was answered with a split-payment offer and the call ended with a follow-up booked for noon next day.

review.reason: Highest script score: use it in training
review.summary: S., 27, calling from Istanbul, is in a stalled situationship with a man who says he cannot commit because of money, wants marriage and a family, and lost an earlier partner to cancer. Brianna ran a strong discovery and a four-pillar pitch, but the scale check came back uncertain and she quoted $14K anyway. S. asked for a trial, Brianna improvised a $1K single session and pushed hard on her need to think it over, and S. ended the call asking for two or three days with nothing paid.

review.reason: Critical flag: needs a manager to listen
review.summary: N. is a 31-year-old journeyman pipe fitter, introverted and anxious around women, with one date in about four years and nothing coming from the apps. He wants a partner and confidence. The rep ran a decent discovery, listed the features, quoted $7,200 with financing in the same breath, ran a live credit application including his SSN, and then answered his request for a day or two with 'I already pulled your credit' and 'financing may not be open tomorrow'. He declined and said he felt rushed and pressured.

review.reason: Critical flag: needs a manager to listen
review.summary: J., 37, on the autism spectrum, has never been in a relationship, is currently without income (he made $18,000 last year) and originally wanted to be in Kim's matchmaking database. Mariah spent half the call challenging his motivation and urgency, quoted $7,200 with Klarna or in-house options in the same breath, and when he said he could not afford it she built a $300 deposit and a 24-month ClarityPay loan, telling him to put at least $30,000 on the application. He signed the financing while saying he was scared.

M., 36, a travelling irrigation technician in Florida, has been single for 11 years after being cheated on, has had mixed results putting himself out there this past year and fears he is not mentally ready for a relationship. Makena ran a long discovery that argued with several of his answers, did not pitch the pillars, then offered either $3,800 for six calls or a discounted $1K two-call start. He said he would think about it, answered the belief check well, and ended by saying the two calls were all he could do near term.

E., in her 60s and never married, wants companionship and marriage after a long situationship with a radio host and is dating someone new. Ellie ran a long, repetitive discovery that left E. feeling judged, deflected her request for the price for 13 minutes, pitched a three-phase framework, then quoted $7,200 and went straight to splits and ClarityPay credit checks. E. declined on price twice more, said she would think and pray, and the call ended unsold.

C. is a divorced father who has dated for about two and a half years (25 to 30 dates), is confident and socially strong, and wants a long-term partner but has not had a relationship last past a couple of months. He framed his issue as post-rejection anxiety he does not think is a problem. The rep concluded early that she could not pinpoint anything to work on, never explored cost or the picture a year out, never pitched, and ended by suggesting he watch his next 3 to 6 months and reconnect in a couple of weeks.

M., a single man from the Midwest with a physical disability, a history of an abusive relationship and a recent layoff, wants strategies for approaching women and reading signals. Ellie ran a long discovery, delivered a generic three-phase pitch with guarantee-style reassurance, never stated the program price, and when he said he could not commit she improvised a $1,000 one-call deposit, then split it and took $100 on the call.

exemplary.quote: Let me know as soon as you got that text because sometimes it doesn't go through.
exemplary.why: Confirms the connect-to-closer text landed while still on the phone.

exemplary.quote: So, if we just put aside the relationship with her at the moment, do you feel like you'll be able to really kind of move forward and move on?
exemplary.why: The screening question that surfaced the real fit issue.

exemplary.quote: I'm not sure that this might be the right path for you at this time to work with her.
exemplary.why: Honest, kind disqualification with a path to keep following Kimberly.

exemplary.quote: I do want to be very clear, though. Like, this is not a matchmaking service.
exemplary.why: Corrected an expectation mismatch (he wanted to be set up with someone) early.

exemplary.quote: I'm going to stay on the phone with you so I can make sure you receive that.
exemplary.why: Stayed on the line while the intro text to the closer was sent.

exemplary.quote: When you say you mess everything up, what do you do?
exemplary.why: Asks for specifics behind a vague self-label.

exemplary.quote: I can't give an exact number because it's, it's completely dependent on you.
exemplary.why: Holds the anchor when he asks what four figures means, without giving a specific price, and moves him to McKenna.

exemplary.quote: So do you really want to try and fight for this relationship or are you just really kind of needing more assistance on letting go and moving on?
exemplary.why: Clarifies what he actually wants help with before selling the call.

exemplary.quote: When you say it wasn't the right matches, what do you mean by that?
exemplary.why: Digs into a vague answer to get the real issue.

exemplary.quote: I don't want you to get on the call with McKenna and that end up not being an option.
exemplary.why: Declines to book a call that might not fit what the lead asked for rather than overselling.

exemplary.quote: How has this really been affecting your confidence now?
exemplary.why: Goes to the emotional cost, drawing out her 'bad picker' self-doubt.

exemplary.quote: I'm gonna text you McKenna's phone number because she would be the person of course that you'd be having the meeting with and that way you guys are connected beforehand
exemplary.why: Connects lead to closer before the call and gives her an action that confirms the booking.

playbook.name: Kimberly Rae Coaching: Master Closing Doc

checks.text: States the call is confidential
Discloses the call is recorded
Credibility: has taken hundreds of these calls
Invites full transparency
Frames the goal of the call and gets agreement
References setter notes (or Kim's DM notes) so they feel seen
Opens with why they took an hour out of their day
Asks the biggest thing not working in dating/relationships
Asks what they mean, in their own words
Asks if anything else is getting in the way
Probes duration (how long, always been this way)
Probes spillover into other areas of life
Relationship status (single, seeing someone, undefined)
Apps usage
Work and meeting people organically
How long actively dating
Flexes the call to the segment (novice, achiever, rebuilder, returner)
Gets weekly mechanics (apps time, conversations, dates)
Asks where it usually falls apart
Asks what they have tried (apps, coaching, books, therapy)
Asks how that went
Asks what they think has been getting in the way
Does not correct the belief yet (saves it for the pitch)
Asks why now vs six months ago
Asks what it has been costing them, beyond dating
Goes deeper with a segment-aware cost question
Magic wand: what changes if this were solved
Lets silence breathe instead of rushing
Asks them to paint the picture a year from now
Asks why that is important to them
Asks what part they most look forward to
Asks if there is anything else they should know
Reflects their situation back and gets permission to walk through how Kim helps
High-level promise of process and visible change, no outcome guarantee
Pillar 1, The Honest Read, tied to what they've tried
Pillar 2, The Reset (profile, photos, messaging)
Pillar 3, The Inner Game
Pillar 4, Read & Lead
Delivery: group calls twice weekly, library, community, 1:1 for paid tiers
Checks for questions or understanding
Asks how they feel about the process
Uses the 1 to 10 scale when the answer is uncertain
Handles what keeps them from 9 or 10 before price
Paints getting started before revealing the investment
Recommends one tier based on discovery
Ties the recommendation to what they said
States the price and stays silent
Does not dump all tiers
Takes money off the table and checks belief in the process first
Tie-down: 'not should I, but how do I make this work'
Does not hand out payment plans to an uncertainty objection
Confirms who they're speaking to and introduces self as Kimberly's team
Anchors to what the lead did (application, quiz, training, DM)
Explains the purpose (point them in the right direction)
Gets permission to ask a few questions
Biggest thing not working in dating/relationships
Digs in: what does that look like, how long
Relationship status / background
What they've tried and how it went
Doubt: what's getting in the way
Why now

Desired picture if solved
Reflects their situation back in one line
Sells the consultation call (worst case clarity, best case changes it)

Handles hesitation with the resourcefulness reframe or financing/credit check
Offers a live transfer or two specific times
Confirms timezone and email
Has them accept the calendar invite while on the phone
Gets their word to reschedule rather than no-show
Quiet place, present, not driving
Connects them to the closer (intro text) and/or sends the pre-call video
